newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called steady ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called steady ahead of weekend.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open mostly steady Friday despite talk of softer cash prices ahead of the weekend, trade sources said.
September over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.42 to $2.435 at 0930 EDT from $2.41-2.42 earlier in the session.
The contract settled Thursday at $2.428 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, September last traded 0.2 cent lower at $2.426.
Early cash prices at Henry Hub were talked several cents lower at $2.45-2.48.
However, electricity prices in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool were quoted about $10 higher at $33.00-34.00 per megawatt hour.

Technical traders pegged September resistance at $2.55 and then at the contract high and double top at $2.605 and $2.64-2.655. Support was seen at $2.34 and $2.30, with better buying likely at $2.25-2.27.

In Thursday's cash, Gulf Coast prices jumped more than 10 cents to the low-to-mid $2.50s. Midcon pipes were up a similar amount to the low-to-mid $2.40s. New York city gate gas gained 10-15 cents to the low-to-mid $2.70s.

Despite the expected arrival of warmer weather this weekend throughout the Northeast and Midwest, temperatures are forecast to return to cooler levels by early next week, according to Weather Services Corp.
